title: Training Object Permanence in World Models
abstract: Object permanence and solidity are hallmarks of human cognitive priors. Recent studies show that video generation models, a paradigmatic class of current world models, have begun to show emerged reasoning abilities, making them ideal candidates for building human-like physical intelligence. Do video models have emerged object permanence in them? If not, could we train them with a core-cognition inspired dataset? We introduce WROP (World Reasoning with Object Permanence), a data infrastructure of 150 hand-designed cognitive science inspired tasks, divided into six cognitive categories. We build Blender generators that randomize speed, lighting, camera angle, and other nuisance parameters while preserving each task's cognitive structure, yielding 10,000+ samples per task. We release a 1.5M-sample training corpus and a 300-question exam. On this exam we evaluate 14 video models: 3 reference-to-video, 7 edit, and 4 continuation, among which PWM-WROP, our 16B world model. In a blind pairwise Elo study, PWM-WROP ranks first among continuation models and third overall, behind only a statistical tie between two reference-to-video models. We release the data, exam, model answers, scores, weights, and PWM, our native-PyTorch training stack on AWS Trainium2.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In Computer Vision and Neural Networks, today's lecture is on Object-Permanence.World: Training Object Permanence in World Models. Recent work such as Video-R1 and A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite reflects a shift from generating attractive clips toward testing whether systems reason across time. This paper, from a broad collaboration including the University of Southern California and Carnegie Mellon University, focuses on continuity and elementary physics. If a video model cannot keep track of a hidden ball, can we trust it as a world model? Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 在计算机视觉和神经网络领域，今天的讲座主题是物体恒存性。World：在世界模型中训练物体恒存性。最近的一些工作，比如Video-R1和A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite，反映出一种转变：从生成好看的视频片段，转向测试系统是否能跨时间进行推理。这篇论文来自一个广泛的合作团队，包括南加州大学和卡内基梅隆大学，聚焦于连续性和基础物理。如果一个视频模型连一个被藏起来的球都追踪不了，我们还能把它当作世界模型来信任吗？好，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi, Professor. What does object permanence mean in a generated video?
segments.zh: 教授您好，在生成的视频里，客体永久性是什么意思？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It means expecting an object to continue existing even when it cannot be seen, and to reappear with its identity and location consistent with what happened before. The paper pairs that idea with object solidity: solid objects should not pass through one another, and contact should have consequences. Its benchmark tests these expectations through occlusion, moving containers, apertures, support removal, and collisions. Think of these as basic rules a video model needs before more elaborate physical reasoning can be credible.
segments.zh: 它指的是，一个物体即使看不见了，也应该继续存在，并且再次出现时，它的身份和位置要跟之前发生的事情保持一致。论文把这个概念和物体实体性配成一对：实体物体不应该互相穿过，接触应该产生后果。它的基准通过遮挡、移动容器、孔洞、支撑移除和碰撞来测试这些预期。你可以把这些看成视频模型需要掌握的基本规则，有了它们，更复杂的物理推理才站得住脚。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So permanence is about tracking hidden objects, while solidity is about what happens when objects meet?
segments.zh: 所以永久性关注的是追踪被遮挡的物体，而固体性关注的是物体相遇时会发生什么？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. The benchmark, called W-R-O-P, separates those challenges into 6 task families. Three test permanence: an object passing behind an occluder, a moving screen revealing an unchanged arrangement, and an object staying associated with a container as it moves. The other 3 test solidity: whether an object fits through an aperture, falls when support is removed, and maintains its identity through a collision. That separation helps reveal which kinds of physical consistency a model has learned.
segments.zh: 没错。这个叫WROP的基准把这些挑战分成了6个任务族。三个测试永久性：物体从遮挡物后面经过、移动的屏幕揭开一个没变的排列、以及物体在移动时始终和某个容器保持关联。另外三个测试固体性：物体能不能穿过一个孔、支撑被移除后会不会掉落、以及碰撞后还能不能保持自己的身份。这种拆分有助于揭示模型到底学到了哪几种物理一致性。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The team built 150 Blender scene generators, with 10,000 samples from each, for about 1.5 million animations. Each clip has 120 frames at 24 frames per second, split into 60 frames of context and 60 frames of continuation. The scenes vary meaningful properties, like object geometry and aperture size, as well as nuisance properties, like color, lighting, and camera angle. This is like testing a student on the same principle under different conditions, rather than letting them memorize one answer.
segments.zh: 团队用Blender做了150个场景生成器，每个生成1万个样本，总共大约150万段动画。每段视频120帧、每秒24帧，前60帧是上下文，后60帧是延续部分。场景里既有真正有意义的变量，比如物体几何形状和开口大小，也有无关变量，比如颜色、光照和相机角度。这就像是在不同条件下考学生同一个原理，而不是让他们死记一个答案。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: are these scenes produced by a physics simulator?
segments.zh: 快速问一下，这些场景是用物理模拟器生成的吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. The animations use Blender keyframes, not a rigid-body physics engine. That gives the authors precise control over when an object disappears, reappears, or contacts another object, but it means physical plausibility depends on manual scene design and inspection. For training, the team fine-tuned a 16-billion-parameter continuation model from Cosmos Three Nano. It received 57 conditioning frames and predicted 60 frames, training for one epoch at 320 by 192 resolution.
segments.zh: 不是。这些动画用的是 Blender 关键帧，不是刚体物理引擎。这样作者就能精确控制物体什么时候消失、重新出现，或者和另一个物体接触，但这也意味着物理合理性取决于手动设计场景和人工检查。训练方面，团队基于 Cosmos Three Nano 微调了一个 160 亿参数的续写模型。模型接收 57 帧条件帧，预测 60 帧，以 320×192 的分辨率训练了一个 epoch。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How did they judge whether a continuation was physically plausible rather than merely visually similar?
segments.zh: 他们怎么判断一段延续在物理上是合理的，而不只是看起来相似？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Human judgment was the primary measure. Twenty raters compared anonymized outputs for text alignment, motion quality, physical plausibility, and object permanence. The authors also calculated image-similarity metrics, but treated them as secondary: a frame can resemble the reference while still showing an impossible event. In the overall ranking, the trained model placed third and was the highest-ranked true-continuation system. Two reference-to-video systems tied for first, though their different interfaces complicate direct comparisons.
segments.zh: 人类判断是主要衡量标准。二十位评分者比较了匿名输出，从文本对齐、运动质量、物理合理性和物体恒存性几个方面打分。作者也计算了图像相似度指标，但只把它们当作次要参考：一帧画面可能看起来和参考很像，却仍然展示了不可能发生的事件。在总排名中，训练后的模型位列第三，是排名最高的真实续写系统。两个参考图生视频系统并列第一，不过它们界面不同，很难直接比较。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The task breakdown is useful beyond a single leaderboard. A robotics or simulation team could use these controlled scenes to probe whether a video model preserves object identity, tracks items inside moving containers, or predicts a fall after support is removed. Those are relevant checks when a system must maintain a coherent scene over time. The benchmark does not establish that a model can safely control a robot, but it can expose specific weaknesses before researchers rely on generated video as a planning signal.
segments.zh: 这种任务拆解的价值不止于一张排行榜。机器人或仿真团队可以用这些受控场景来检验视频模型是否能保持物体身份、追踪移动容器里的物品，或者预测支撑移除后的坠落。当系统必须在时间维度上维持连贯场景时，这些都是相关的检查。这个基准并不能证明模型可以安全地控制机器人，但它能在研究人员把生成视频当作规划信号之前，暴露出具体的弱点。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: PWM-WROP did especially well on permanence, but why was collision harder?
segments.zh: PWM-WROP在永久性上表现特别好，但为什么碰撞更难呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The results suggest that keeping track of hidden objects and reasoning about contact are distinct demands. The trained model ranked first on static-scene occlusion, third on dynamic occlusion and container permanence, and second on object drop. But it ranked fifth on obstruction and eighth on collision. Other systems led some contact tasks. This pattern cautions against treating one aggregate score as a complete measure of physical understanding; a model may maintain identities yet still mishandle how objects interact.
segments.zh: 结果表明，追踪隐藏物体和对接触进行推理是两种不同的能力要求。训练后的模型在静态场景遮挡上排名第一，在动态遮挡和容器永久性上排名第三，在物体掉落上排名第二。但在障碍物上排名第五，在碰撞上排名第八。其他系统在一些接触任务上领先。这一模式提醒我们，不要把单一的综合得分当作衡量物理理解能力的完整标准；一个模型可能能维持物体身份，却仍然处理不好物体之间如何相互作用。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That distinction connects to a broader trend. Video-R1 explores temporal reasoning in multimodal language models, while A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite emphasizes evaluating reasoning rather than visual quality alone. This paper shifts attention toward persistent object representations in generated continuations, using controlled three-dimensional events and human ratings. Its contribution is not proof of a general internal physics engine; it is a way to ask more targeted questions about what a model keeps track of and how it updates a scene.
segments.zh: 这一区分关联到一个更广泛的趋势。Video-R1探索多模态语言模型中的时序推理，而A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite则强调评估推理能力，而不只是视觉质量。这篇论文把注意力转向生成续帧中的持久物体表征，使用受控的三维事件和人工评分。它的贡献并不是证明模型内部存在一个通用的物理引擎，而是提供了一种方法，让我们能更有针对性地追问：模型到底在追踪什么，又是如何更新场景的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: What would researchers need to test before claiming these gains generalize to the real world?
segments.zh: 研究人员需要测试什么，才能声称这些收益能泛化到现实世界？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: They would need larger human evaluations, natural video, longer time horizons, and mechanisms not seen during training. The exam has 300 questions, and the models differ in interface, resolution, and sampling, so rankings are informative but not perfectly controlled. The synthetic scenes also use manually authored motion rather than general physical simulation. These limits make the benchmark a useful instrument for diagnosis, while leaving open whether its gains transfer to unfamiliar environments or real-world interaction.
segments.zh: 他们需要更大规模的人类评估、自然视频、更长的时间跨度，以及训练中没见过的机制。这个测试有300道题，而且各模型在界面、分辨率和采样上都不一样，所以排名有参考价值，但并不是完全受控的。这些合成场景用的也是人工编写的运动，而不是通用的物理模拟。这些局限让这个基准成为一个有用的诊断工具，但也留下了一个悬而未决的问题：它的收益能否迁移到不熟悉的环境或真实世界的交互中。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The central takeaway is that visual continuity and physical continuity are not the same thing. A model can produce a polished clip while losing an object, changing its identity, or disconnecting an event from its cause. W-R-O-P makes those failures easier to isolate, and its results suggest targeted synthetic training can help on specific tasks. The memorable question to carry forward is simple: when the camera cannot see an object, does the model still behave as though the object exists? Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 核心结论是，视觉上的连续和物理上的连续不是一回事。一个模型可以生成一段看起来很精致的视频，却把物体弄丢了、改变了它的身份，或者让事件和原因脱节。W-R-O-P 让这些失败更容易被单独拎出来，而它的结果也说明，有针对性的合成训练能在特定任务上帮上忙。最值得记住、也最该带走的一个问题很简单：当镜头看不到某个物体时，模型还会不会表现得好像那个物体依然存在？感谢收听。如果还有别的问题，可以问我们的 AI 助手，或者留言评论。
